newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN HOUSING DEPT TO EMPLOY CONSULTANTS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN HOUSING DEPT TO EMPLOY CONSULTANTS.

text.p: South Africa's Department of Housing planned to employ consultants to assess the government's housing asset portfolio worth about 12 billion rand, director-general Billy Cobbett said on Wednesday.
He told the parliamentary public accounts committee that although this would "add to the litany of criticism about the use of consultants", his department did not have the capacity to do it itself.
"(My) department does not have, and is unlikely ever to have the necessary staff, skills and expertise to manage an asset portfolio of 12 billion rand," Cobbett said.
Earlier this month the government came under fire for its increasing use of consultants which was seen costing the country more than a billion rand a year.

On Wednesday Deputy Auditor-General Bertie Loots said the problems faced with the housing fund were a reflection of the state of affairs which several other government funds inherited from the apartheid era.
"Billions of rands of taxpayers' money are not under effective control due to various factors, including the inability to prepare proper financial statements...(since) March 1994," he said.
He said it was clear that attempts to get departments themselves to resolve the situation would not solve the problem.
The housing portfolio, held in the National Housing Fund, consists of loans worth about 9.7 billion rand to local authorities and property and individual loans worth about 1.8 billion rand.
It was amassed over the last approximately 10 years by the various housing authorities under the previous government and after the assessment will be devolved to local authorities.
